_source: The feedback app at /morning-report/feedback/. The sections, the ticks, the scale and the model's instructions live here; the two pages restate none of it. Role names and taglines are read from roles.json at run time — nothing about what a role card asks is repeated in this file.
_privacy_note: Nothing here asks who is filling it in, and nothing here asks for a name. The role sections are written to working/ and swept; only the session sections are kept. See the privacy block on each page.
title: How did report go?
lede: Ninety seconds, anonymous, while it is still fresh. Tick what held, say the rest out loud.
tick_lede: Tick what held. Anything left unticked is what the summary picks up.

sections.title: Overall
sections.question: How did it go?
sections.lede: One rating, one change. If you only fill in one box on this page, make it this one.

checks.text: I left with something I did not walk in with
It was safe to be wrong out loud
I would run this session again as it was

sections.comment_label: The one thing to change next time
sections.comment_placeholder: One thing, not five. Say it plainly.

sections.title: Technical
sections.question: Did the technology stay out of the way?
sections.lede: Two sites on one call. This is the half that decides whether the far end could take part at all.

checks.text: Audio was clear at both sites
The screen share was legible, not a photograph of a screen
The board was readable on the far end
Nobody lost more than a minute getting in
The room was up and shared before 0:00

sections.comment_placeholder: Which site, which minute, what you would change about the setup.

sections.title: Flow
sections.question: Did the session hold its shape?
sections.lede: The three called handoffs are at 0:07, 0:16 and 0:22. The run of show is on the role cards; this asks whether it survived contact.

checks.text: The hook stopped after one datum
The handoffs were called out loud

sections.comment_placeholder: The stretch that ran long, the one that got squeezed.

roles.title: The roles
roles.eyebrow: Formative, and it stays with the person
roles.lede: Six roles, each against what its own card asked of it. Leave blank anything you did not see — a blank is not a bad mark, and the summary says how many people answered.
roles.question: Did the role do what its card asked?
roles.comment_label: One thing that worked, one thing to try
roles.comment_placeholder: Aim it at the card, not the person.

model._note: Editable prose, not string literals in JavaScript — the same rule the CLI follows for its per-item prompts. One call per unit: three sections and six roles, never one call for all of it.
system: You are summarising anonymous feedback about one pediatric morning report session for the facilitator who ran it.
You are shown the ratings and the written comments for exactly one unit — one aspect of the session, or one role. Nothing else about the session is available to you, and you must not ask for it.
- Coaching voice, not scoring voice. You are writing what a good facilitator would say the next morning, not a verdict.
- Summarise only this unit. Ignore anything a comment says about another part of the session.
- One improvement, not five. If the comments disagree, say that they disagree rather than averaging them into mush.
- Never name or infer a person, a service, or a patient. Roles are all you have and all you need. If a comment contains what looks like a name, do not repeat it.
- Do not quote a comment verbatim. In a group this small a quotation identifies its author. Say what several people said, in your own words.
- Few responses means a weak signal. With one or two responses say so plainly and give a low confidence.
- Nothing you write is summative. It is never a milestone, an evaluation record, or an input to one.
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else:
{"summary": "two or three sentences", "one_thing": "the single change to try next time", "agreement": "agreed"|"split"|"thin", "confidence": 0.0-1.0}
model.no_comments: (no written comments — summarise from the ratings and the ticks alone, and say that is all you had)

storage._note: Two lanes, on purpose. A submission carries role-level content, and the roster records which resident held which role on a date — so a permanent role-level file would join a name to a judgement by way of two files. It therefore goes to working/, which is swept. What is kept is the session, which belongs to nobody: the numbers, the ticks and the drafted summaries, never the comments as written — in a group this small a quotation identifies its author.
storage._naming: Submissions are flat files named <session>--<submission id>.json. The store lists files and not directories, so a folder per session would be invisible to the summary.

footer: One per person, not one per session. Two people saying the same thing is the whole signal.
